title: October 2026 Microsoft Patch Tuesday | Tenable®
summary: Microsoft patched 1,407 CVEs in October, its largest Patch Tuesday release to date, including two zero-day flaws, one exploited in the wild: CVE-2026-96951.

**Microsoft addresses 1407 CVEs in the tenth Patch Tuesday of 2026, marking the second consecutive month to reset the bar as the largest Patch Tuesday release. This month’s updates include patches for two zero days, including one that was exploited in the wild.**


Microsoft patched 1,407 CVEs in its October 2026 Patch Tuesday release, with 69 rated critical, 1,337 rated as important, and one rated as low.


This month’s update includes patches for 301 products and components. The following table lists the products with the most CVEs patched this month. A full list of patched products is available in the appendix.

Elevation of Privilege (EoP) vulnerabilities accounted for 47.9% of the vulnerabilities patched this month, followed by remote code execution (RCE) vulnerabilities at 22.3%.


Important


## CVE-2026-96951 | Windows Shell security feature bypass vulnerability


[CVE-2026-96951](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2026-96951) is a security feature bypass vulnerability affecting Windows Shell. It received a CVSSv3 score of 8.8 and was rated as important. According to Microsoft, this vulnerability was exploited in the wild as a zero-day.


An attacker could exploit this vulnerability using social engineering tactics, via email or messages, to convince their target to open a malicious file. Successful exploitation would bypass the Mark of the Web (MOTW) security feature.


This is the third flaw in Windows Shell that was exploited in the wild in 2026:[CVE-2026-21510](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-21510) was patched in[February 2026’s Patch Tuesday](https://www.tenable.com/blog/microsofts-february-2026-patch-tuesday-addresses-54-cves-cve-2026-21510-cve-2026-21513) while[CVE-2026-32202](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2026-32202) was patched in[April 2026’s Patch Tuesday](https://www.tenable.com/blog/microsofts-april-2026-patch-tuesday-addresses-163-cves-cve-2026-32201) .


Important


## CVE-2026-108398 |.NET Framework security feature bypass vulnerability


[CVE-2026-108398](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2026-108398) is a security feature bypass vulnerability affecting.NET Framework. It received a CVSSv3 score of 8.8 and is rated as important. It was publicly disclosed prior to a patch being available.


An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by registering a malicious.NET assembly on a vulnerable system to be loaded by a protected process. Successful exploitation would allow the attacker to bypass Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC).


Critical


## CVE-2026-70229 | Windows Active Directory Domain Services remote code execution vulnerability


[CVE-2026-70229](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2026-70229) is an RCE vulnerability affecting Windows Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS). It received a CVSSv3 score of 8.1 and is rated as critical. Microsoft assesses this vulnerability as “Exploitation More Likely” according to[Microsoft’s Exploitability Index](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/msrc/exploitability-index) .


An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a crafted packet to the vulnerable AD DS service. Successful exploitation could grant an attacker code execution on the vulnerable system.


Important


## CVE-2026-70279 | Microsoft Exchange Server spoofing vulnerability


[CVE-2026-70279](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2026-70279) is a spoofing vulnerability affecting Microsoft Exchange Server. It received a CVSSv3 score of 9.3 and is rated as important. It was assessed as “Exploitation More Likely.” An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by convincing a target through social engineering to click on a malicious link. Successful exploitation against a target with administrative privileges would allow an attacker to access or modify organizational data.


Critical


## CVE-2026-70571 | Microsoft Exchange Server remote code execution vulnerability


[CVE-2026-70571](https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/en-US/vulnerability/CVE-2026-70571) is a remote code execution vulnerability affecting Microsoft Exchange Server. It received a CVSSv3 score of 8.1 and is rated as critical. It was assessed as “Exploitation More Likely.”


An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a malicious email to a vulnerable Microsoft Exchange server that would cause it to process the email using internal content-conversion. Successful exploitation would allow an attacker the ability to execute code on the Exchange server.

## Windows Server 2012 End of Support


On October 13, the final year of[Extended Security Updates (ESU)](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/windows-server-2012) for Windows Server 2012 and Windows Server 2012 R2 ended. Microsoft will no longer release security updates for either version. To identify unsupported versions of Windows Server 2012, customers can use[plugin ID 192813](https://www.tenable.com/plugins/nessus/192813) . To check the ESU status of Windows Server 2012 and 2012 R2 hosts, customers can use[plugin ID 182965](https://www.tenable.com/plugins/nessus/182965) .


Extended support for Windows 10 Enterprise 2016 Long-Term Servicing Branch (LTSB) and Windows 10 IoT Enterprise LTSB 2016 also ended on October 13. To identify Windows 10 Enterprise 2016 LTSB, customers can use[plugin ID 192817](https://www.tenable.com/plugins/nessus/192817) .


## Windows Server 2022 End of Mainstream Support


October 13, 2026 marks the end of mainstream support for Windows Server 2022. This month’s security update is the last one issued under mainstream support. The product now enters extended support, where it will continue receiving monthly security updates at no additional cost through October 14, 2031. Organizations still running Windows Server 2022 can begin evaluating an upgrade path to Windows Server 2025, the current LTSC release, which carries mainstream support through November 2029 and extended support through November 2034.


## Additional Microsoft Products End of Support


As of October 13, several Microsoft products have reached end of support. Since these products will no longer receive security updates, we recommend upgrading to supported versions as soon as possible.


- [Office 2021](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/lifecycle/products/office-2021)
